title: Backfill or formally waive verification evidence on epic-21 'done' stories — 16 files ship an all-unchecked task list and an empty Dev Agent Record
why: All 16 epic-21 stories carry 'Status: done' yet every Tasks/Subtasks checkbox in every file is unchecked ('- [ ]', never '- [x]') and every Dev Agent Record section is the unfilled template stub (blank 'Agent Model Used' / 'Completion Notes List' / 'Change Log' headers, no content) — in sharp contrast to every DNI-32x/33x/34x/35x/37x/38x story in this same batch, which carries a populated file list, dated change log, and test-run counts (e.g. 'flutter test — 1810 passing'). Grepping lib/ shows the epic-21 feature set (device registry, per-account DB isolation, session persistence, account picker, tiered deletion, the onUserDeleted cloud function) genuinely exists, so the work itself was not skipped — but the documents supply no verifiable completion trail a reviewer or future incident investigator could check the 'done' claim against, unlike every other done/review story in the folder.
recommendation: Not worth rewriting 16 historical files retroactively. Forward-looking fix: make the story-authoring skill (or a docs-triage Rule-0 checker) refuse Status: done/review when Tasks/Subtasks still contain an unchecked '- [ ]' line or the Dev Agent Record section is the unfilled template — this is exactly the discipline the later Epic-25+ process already adopted by convention; enforce it instead of leaving it as convention.
acceptance_criteria: A checker (doc-lint or make audit rule) fails when a docs/stories/implementation/*.md has Status: done/review and still contains an unchecked '- [ ]' line in Tasks/Subtasks, or a Dev Agent Record section with only empty headers.
New stories merged after this finding are not left with Status: done and a blank Dev Agent Record.

corrections: Minor: the illustrative 'flutter test — 1810 passing' quote in the narrative isn't a literal citation (real DNI counts are 1766-1934); it's approximate color, not part of the structured evidence array, and doesn't affect the verified core claim.
